lines.text: Fourteen years later Paul went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus, and spoke privately to those recognized as leaders.
Titus, who was with Paul, was not compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.
False brothers came in to spy on their freedom in Christ in order to protect them, but Paul did not give in.
The leaders saw that Paul was entrusted to preach the gospel to the Gentiles, just as Peter was to the Egyptians.
James, Cephas, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship and asked them to remember the poor.
